comparator.name: Information Science (Informatiekunde)
comparator.academicYear: 2026–27 UvA curriculum and study guide, checked 2026-09-26
comparator.sourceNotes: The official 2026–27 curriculum and one-page curriculum scheme establish a 60-EC first year. The first half of Year 2 contains 24 EC of taught courses, a 5-EC project and a 1-EC reflection practicum. In the second half, the published scheme places Regulatory Compliant Information Systems, Semantic Web and Recommender Systems concurrently before Research Methods for Interactive Systems and Applied Machine Learning; a 60-EC year permits two of the three concurrent 6-EC choices. This pathway selects the first two officially listed concurrent choices—Regulatory Compliant Information Systems and Semantic Web—then includes the two later courses, the 5-EC system project and 1-EC practicum. Year 3 similarly contains 30 EC genuine open choice, an 18-EC final project and a 12-EC selection from three listed 6-EC courses; this pathway selects the first two officially listed courses, Social Robotics and Logic and Society, rather than combining all three. The study guide confirms 180 EC, three years, Dutch, and full-time status.

alternatives.label: Information systems, data and digital society
alternatives.concept: Combines programming, databases, data science and computational methods with user-centred design, organisational change, research methods and responsible digital governance. It follows UvA's broad people-data-technology orientation while acknowledging that UCR lacks its dedicated semantic-web, regulatory-systems, social-robotics and compulsory project sequence.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum gives comparable weight to computational information systems, data analysis, organisations, users and the societal implications of digital technology.
progression: All formal prerequisites occur in earlier semesters and every course is assigned to a planned 2026–29 offering. Research and organisational foundations precede advanced methods, algorithms, AI and digital-transformation work; six 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Data science and computational information
alternatives.concept: Retains programming, databases, organisational context and responsible technology while shifting 30 EC toward linear algebra, numerical and systems modelling, probability and advanced machine learning. This route develops the programme's explicit Data Science direction rather than treating information science as software engineering alone.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed schedule adds four mathematics and data courses and removes four design, qualitative and organisational courses, making data modelling the dominant differentiating strand.
alternatives.distinctness: Linear Algebra, Computational & Numerical Methods, Linear Systems and Probability & Statistics replace Consumer Product Design, Qualitative Research Methodology, Psychology of Organizations & Leadership and Persuasive Communication. Each curriculum therefore contains 30 EC absent from the other.
progression: All formal prerequisites occur in earlier semesters and every course is assigned to a planned 2026–29 offering. Mathematical Methods precedes linear algebra, numerical methods and probability; programming precedes advanced algorithms and AI optimisation; six 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Human-centred and socio-technical systems
alternatives.concept: Retains programming, databases, data science and organisational analysis but shifts the advanced programme toward perception, social psychology, interaction, language, institutional trust and technology adoption. It develops the explicit Human-Computer Interaction and Socio-Technical Systems directions as one coherent study of how people and institutions use and respond to digital systems.
alternatives.labelReason: The final curriculum combines a technical information-system foundation with a sustained psychology, cognition, sociology, user-design and organisational sequence.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest programme, Introduction to Brain & Behavior, Social Psychology, Modern Sociology, Perception & Action, Higher Order Functions, New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory and Psycholinguistics replace Mathematical Methods, Logic & Discrete Mathematics, Qualitative Research Methodology, Ethics, Algorithms & Data Structures, Optimization Methods in AI and Neural Networks & Deep Learning. The 52.5-EC shift creates a human-centred socio-technical curriculum and also exceeds the pairwise 30-EC floor against the data-science alternative.
progression: All formal prerequisites occur in earlier semesters and every course is assigned to a planned 2026–29 offering. Introduction to Brain & Behavior precedes the cognitive-science courses; Introduction to Sociology and Modern Sociology precede the advanced social-theory course as an advisory progression; six 300-level courses are included.

selection.assessment: The closest broad Information Science response is feasible. The official Data Science and Human-Computer Interaction directions each support a coherent additional curriculum with material course consequences, while Information Systems and Socio-Technical Systems are substantively represented in the closest core. All three included programmes pass the qualitative and pairwise 30-EC distinctness tests, so production stops at the permitted maximum of three.

notes.text: The UvA programme integrates data science, information systems, human-computer interaction and socio-technical systems through dedicated modelling, design, governance, semantic-web, project and final-research components. UCR can combine substantial programming, databases, data analysis, user research, organisational change, cognition and responsible-technology study, but distributes them across computing, business, psychology, sociology, communication and philosophy rather than reproducing UvA's structured Information Science sequence.
